items.prompt: For n unsorted windows, what dominates this implementation's comparison work?

options.text: Only O(1), because each interval has two endpoints.
options.why: The number of intervals still determines ordering and scan work.

options.text: O(n^2), because every output interval is compared with all earlier ones.
options.why: The sorted frontier scan compares only with its last merged output.

options.text: O(log n), because only one final interval may remain.
options.why: Final output size does not remove the input ordering work.

options.text: O(n log n) sorting, followed by an O(n) scan.
options.why: Every sorted input interval is handled once after the initial sort.

items.explanation: Every sorted input interval is handled once after the initial sort.
